plan.question: How did a shadow war fracture Gaza's control?

chapters.title: The Fracture
beats: By 2024, the scale of the conflict had shifted, with Israel's Rafah offensive marking the beginning of a new phase where local militias began to operate in the void left by the war.

chapters.title: The Players
beats: Yasser Abu Shabab emerged as the face of the Popular Forces, a paramilitary group that positioned itself as a protector of the local population against both Hamas and Israel.
Issam Nabahin was a key operative within this network, tasked with securing aid and maintaining order in the southern zones.

chapters.title: The First Shot
beats: In May 2024, the start of Israel's Rafah offensive coincided with the formal beginning of Popular Forces activity in the Gaza Strip.
By June 2024, the Popular Forces escalated their challenge by launching an attack on a Hamas facility located inside the Khan Yunis University College of Applied Sciences.
This strike signaled that Abu Shabab's group was no longer passive but was actively targeting Hamas infrastructure to establish its own territory.

chapters.title: The Ambush
chapters.bridge: The focus shifts to the security crackdown in the south.
beats: In September 2024, Hamas attempted to assassinate Abu Shabab by firing approximately 90 bullets at his vehicle in a desperate ambush.
During this failed attempt, Islam Hijazi was mistakenly killed, highlighting the chaotic and indiscriminate nature of the internal violence.
In response, a Hamas security unit carried out a military operation against the looters in Khan Yunis and Rafah, killing at least 20 of the perpetrators.

chapters.title: The Split
beats: In January 2025, the fragmentation deepened as two small armed groups, the Abu Khammash and Abu Moghaiseb factions, were formed in Dier al-Balah.
Hamas executed one of Abu Shabab's senior aides in Dier al-Balah, a direct message of intolerance for his growing influence.
By March 2025, Hamas clashed directly with the Abu Khammash and Abu Moghaiseb factions in Dier al-Balah, showing the conflict had spread beyond the main capital.
On 13 April 2025, a group of Popular Forces members were ambushed by Hamas fighters in southern Rafah, marking the end of any remaining truce between the two sides.

chapters.title: Blood in the Streets
beats: On 14 April 2025, the house at the site of the previous ambush was destroyed by an Israeli airstrike, further blurring the lines between the factions.
In May 2025, the Popular Forces were reported to be securing aid convoys, including vehicles of the United Nations and the Red Cross, at the Kerem Shalom crossing.
Hamas accused Abu Shabab of being a collaborator with Israel, while Israel revealed on 5 June 2025 that it had been backing the Popular Forces.
On 9 June 2025, Popular Forces gunmen opened fire at a crowd of Palestinians walking to an aid distribution centre, and Hamas forces ambushed a car transporting Issam Nabahin.
The violence escalated as Popular Forces ambushed the Arrow Unit, a special law enforcement unit, killing 6 officers on 11 June 2025.
An Israeli drone bombed Issam Nabahin's detention cell on 11 June 2025, but he posted a video on 18 June 2025 confirming he was alive.
On 27 June 2025, the Popular Forces seized control of Nasser Hospital after a gunbattle with Hamas forces in Khan Yunis.
Hamas ordered Abu Shabab to turn himself in on 2 July 2025, and he admitted on 6 July 2025 that the Popular Forces had Israeli backing.

chapters.title: The Aftermath
beats: In August 2025, Issam Nabahin posted a video stating he was back in Popular Forces-controlled eastern Rafah, indicating the group remained a significant force.
Hamas-led authorities executed three men who allegedly had ties with Abu Shabab outside Al-Shifa Hospital on 21 September 2025.
A Popular Forces operative was executed by Hamas forces on 28 September 2025, marking the consolidation of Hamas's security grip despite the internal strife.
The Rad'a Force executed six Popular Forces militants in Khan Yunis on 27 July 2025, demonstrating the brutal cost of the internal war.
